stage: P1 ordinary startup candidate, published and verified against origin/main

find_incremental.change: Compact the stock Find window only when its optional wrap control is hidden and the client matches 236 by 74 dialog units. Reuse the common client-geometry restore after refreshing the frame. Requests with a hook or custom template retain their native layout.
find_incremental.published_negative_control: x86/x64 each failed the new stock Find geometry assertion in ANSI and Unicode. The existing termination notification assertions passed.
find_incremental.incremental_candidate: Eight real A/W Find and Replace cases on x86/x64. Each had a styled frame, sent the expected Find Next, Replace and Replace All notifications where applicable, then sent one termination notification. The stock Find geometry passed.
find_incremental.diagnostic: Subtracting native height directly triggered the first non-client recalculation and produced 356x107 rather than the expected 354x101. Refreshing the frame and restoring the desired client rectangle through the common path passed.

file_runtime_followup.result: x86 and x64, eight confirmed selections each across ANSI/Unicode, open/save and native legacy/Explorer modes.
file_runtime_followup.prior_x86_timeout: Not reproduced with the diagnostic probe. Its path and observation work differ from the original fixture; root cause remains unconfirmed.
file_runtime_followup.native_explorer: Both widths observed a DirectUI content area and SHELLDLL_DefView. Save can collapse the shell view to zero height. The installed native layout does not match the static modern 1552 dialog template at run time, so the 40-DLU template difference is not a sufficient resize rule.

folder_runtime.published_shell: 16/16. Both architectures, ANSI/Unicode, the legacy tree and BIF_USENEWUI, selection and cancellation. Existing Win2000 frame attached in each case and the Shell preserved the selected folder PIDL.
folder_runtime.incremental_com: 10/10 startup cases for the folder bridge and prior file fallback: folder selection and result array, folder cancellation, custom folder cancellation, file-open native cancellation, and Win16 folder cancellation, each on both widths.
folder_runtime.shared_contract_tests: The COM controller and common bridge tests passed on both widths. Requests for a filesystem single-file selection use the Explorer path; custom controls, label overrides, callbacks, multiselect and unsupported options retain native Show.
folder_runtime.binary_boundary: The observed new ntw2ks imports are ole32.dll and shell32.dll. All four exported entry points remain identical.

print_incremental.classic: PrintDlg and PageSetupDlg cancel passed 8/8 across both widths and ANSI/Unicode. Each had a Win2000 frame and zero CommDlgExtendedError.
print_incremental.extended: PrintDlgEx cancel passed 4/4 across both widths and ANSI/Unicode. Each had a Win2000 frame, returned S_OK, and set PD_RESULT_CANCEL.
print_incremental.scope: Ordinary desktop, self-owned dialogs, default print device configured. No job submitted. The existing classic extended bridge preserves supported settings. On both widths a native PrintDlgEx comparison produced no dialog observable by the fixture before its timeout. The original printnew.dlg defines a separate General property page; exact visual parity is open.
print_incremental.shared_contract_tests: Classic and extended print contract tests passed on x86 and x64.
print_incremental.confirm: Four PrintDlgEx A/W cases accepted pages 2–4 and returned PD_RESULT_PRINT plus DEVNAMES and DEVMODE. Four cases with PD_RETURNDC returned E_FAIL and no settings. The same four paired Win16 requests returned the same E_FAIL; a Win2000-specific regression was not identified. Apply and custom native fallback are still open. Actual release Apply additionally passed for four A/W cases across both widths, returning the three-copy snapshot after the fixture changed the live field to five copies and closed. Four paired confirmation cases also returned three copies. Settings and handles were freed, with no job submitted.
print_incremental.dc_native_control: With no run16s DLL, PrintDlgW(PD_RETURNDEFAULT | PD_RETURNDC) reported success and returned a null hDC on both widths. Direct CreateDCW using the native DEVNAMES/DEVMODE returned null on both widths. The environment does not provide a usable printer DC; the bridge tests requiring one are not counted as passes.

reference: Windows 2000 English SP2 OEM CD, original setup members under I386. ISO9660 extraction only, no VM boot, modules mapped as resource data only.
find_layout_difference: Stock 1540 adds control 1042 and a helper on Windows 11. In the ordinary native and --2k sample the added control was hidden while its empty row remained. Replace had identical client dimensions between modes.

published_both_arch.file_cancel: 16/16 across x86/x64 for ANSI/Unicode open/save and Explorer/legacy combinations. Result was cancellation with no extended error.
published_both_arch.color_and_font_cancel: all four ANSI/Unicode cases passed for each architecture

file_select.x86: first succeeded, fixture exited 4 while waiting for the next dialog

com_explorer_incremental.initial_failure: The original GetFileName result was an absolute filename. Carrying it unchanged alongside the native folder lost the path in the Explorer dialog: opening failed and saving selected the current directory. Both widths reproduced this.
com_explorer_incremental.fix: For the Explorer path, split fully qualified file paths into the starting directory and filename before calling the system Win32 dialog. Leave relative names and the Win16 bridge unchanged.
com_explorer_incremental.candidate: Eight real Win2000 open/save confirmation and cancellation cases on x86/x64, plus two Win16 open confirmation comparisons. Confirmed the Explorer host, exact returned path, one-item GetResults for open, and HRESULT_FROM_WIN32(ERROR_CANCELLED) for cancellation.
com_explorer_incremental.visual_limit: Uses the installed Win32 Explorer shell layout inside the Win2000 frame. The Windows 2000 original layout is still an open visual item; the Win11 runtime DirectUI hierarchy cannot be resized from the two resource extents alone.

font_color_message_incremental.font: Added scoped native observation to ChooseFontA/W. Both widths confirmed Arial Bold 12-point results and cancellation.
font_color_message_incremental.color: Four native initial-color confirmations and four cancellations. The Windows 2000 source confirms recessed swatch edges; retain the installed native palette for Win2000. No visual match claimed for the expanded palette.
font_color_message_incremental.message: Twelve MessageBox, MessageBoxEx and MessageBoxIndirect A/W native cases on both widths. Each attached and returned IDOK.

expanded_color_p3.reference: The Windows 2000 SP2 and Windows 11 expanded Color templates are both 298 by 184 dialog units. All 27 controls match in position and size except the compact expansion button, which is 140 units wide in SP2 and 138 in Windows 11. The SP2 FillBox implementation draws EDGE_SUNKEN and the default Add action advances from slot 0 to slot 8.
expanded_color_p3.published_contract: The registered --color-expanded fixture passed 8/8 ANSI/Unicode x86/x64 confirmation and cancellation cases against P1. Two RGB edits write back to slots 0 and 8 even on cancel. Confirm changes rgbResult; cancel retains the incoming value. Win2000 frame attached in all eight.
expanded_color_p3.visual_witness: Independent same-thread sampling compared six controls and custom swatch one on both widths. Styled and native control rectangles agreed, including the same one-pixel rounding of three control heights. All eight styled samples and six readable unstyled samples had 195 fill pixels, shadow above, highlight below and the same sampled pixel hash ae1a3c21. The first unstyled sample in each width was unreadable and excluded from the visual comparison.
expanded_color_p3.remaining: The native expanded client measured 447 by 299 pixels. The styled client measured 449 by 305 after expanding from compact mode. The swatch comparison covers one slot against the current OS and the source algorithm; an original Windows 2000 runtime screenshot was not used.
expanded_color_p3.artifact_identity: All eight P1 files matched their recorded SHA-256 at assets and O:/winnt before the run. This test-only change does not rebuild or republish the product.

printer_dc_p4.native_host: Outside the command sandbox, stock PrintDlgW with PD_RETURNDEFAULT and PD_RETURNDC returned a valid printer DC, DEVNAMES and DEVMODE with zero extended error on x86 and x64. All handles were released.
printer_dc_p4.published_contract: Verified the eight published hashes at assets and O:/winnt. On the ordinary host desktop, --2k --print-ex-accept-dc passed for x86 and x64, ANSI and Unicode. Each window was styled and returned S_OK, PD_RESULT_PRINT, a non-null hDC, DEVNAMES and DEVMODE, and pages 2 through 4. The fixture released all three resources.
printer_dc_p4.environment: The earlier null DC is specific to the command sandbox in this comparison. No actual print job was submitted.
printer_dc_p4.native_extended_surface: The exact owned native PrintDlgExW comparison on the normal host saw a visible 0 by 0 ProxyModalWindow owned by the fixture window but belonging to a different process on both widths. Closing that proxy did not return the modal call, so the bounded test terminated its two fixture processes. The published --2k comparison instead exposed a same-process #32770 dialog with printer combo, range, copies, and Apply controls, and cancelled cleanly on both widths. This identifies the broker boundary; it does not establish a property sheet visual match to SP2.
printer_dc_p4.artifact_identity: Test of the existing P1 files. No production change or republication.

client_refinement_p5.color_geometry: Stock Windows caches a 453 by 328 outer rectangle for the expanded picker at 96 DPI before Win2000 attaches. Both the native control and P1 reused it after Define Custom Colors. The resulting client was 447 by 299 native and 449 by 305 styled.
client_refinement_p5.implementation: After the stock button completes its native expansion, require the standard picker controls and the exact old outer extent computed for the dialog DPI. Restore the shared 298 by 184 DLU stock client rectangle while keeping its current screen origin. ChooseColor requests with a caller template use the ordinary observer.
client_refinement_p5.incremental_color: The same strengthened regression fixture failed only the size assertion in 8/8 cases against P1. The incremental candidate passed all eight, including ANSI/Unicode, both widths, confirmation and cancellation, callback, stock geometry and color writeback. Four compact-color confirmations also passed.
client_refinement_p5.incremental_message: Both widths passed all six MessageBox, MessageBoxEx and MessageBoxIndirect A/W entry points with the warning icon, Yes/No/Cancel, the second button selected by DM_GETDEFID, and IDNO returned. The twelve existing OK cases also passed.
client_refinement_p5.page_setup_host: Four PageSetupDlg A/W tests across both widths selected landscape, changed the left margin from 1.0 to 1.25 inches and accepted. Each returned landscape DEVMODE, 11 by 8.5 inch paper dimensions, the edited margin and a DEVNAMES handle. All handles were freed and no print job was sent.
client_refinement_p5.explorer_layout_trial: A stock OPENFILENAME request with OFN_EX_NOPLACESBAR exposed SHELLDLL_DefView without the DirectUI wrapper; it retained native cancellation. A separate OFN_EXPLORER and OFN_ENABLEHOOK trial kept the standard places toolbar (ID 1184) and SHELLDLL_DefView. On the measured 427 by 272 normal-host work area, the trial was clipped in unstyled Windows as well as in P1. In the settled styled sample, the Open button started at x=484, y=313 while the client was 421 by 247. The probe confirmed the legacy host option but the complete with-places layout remains unverified. P5 keeps the existing mode selection.

release.remote_readback: Observed actual origin/main after push. All eight committed asset blobs and both published copies matched the package SHA-256 records. The two production source files also matched their committed blobs.
release.cleanup: Removed the S3-owned clean build and intermediate copied bundles, publishing backups and probe outputs after recording results. No S3 scratch remains under build/t28-package.
release.compiler: C17, MinGW GCC 16.1.0 (i686 UCRT and x86_64 MSVCRT), Ninja 1.13.2, ccache 4.13.6

verification.package: 46/46 grouped ordinary desktop runs after publishing. Owned driver uses --direct. Includes both widths, expanded Color size, message default/icon group, and Win16 open/folder control comparisons.
verification.core: 30/30 focused CTest checks in the clean build, including Win2000 frame lifecycle, local global-style bridge and session style. No administrator global sweep was initiated.
verification.host_printing: Same published package passed PageSetupDlg landscape/margin acceptance 4/4 and PrintDlgEx printer DC acceptance 4/4. No print jobs were sent.
verification.demo: Published x64 demo PE boundary passed. The package demo-pair test was omitted because it requires a private desktop.

client_refinement_p5.file_changes: One appearance helper, one startup adapter, one dialog fixture, and package case markers. Both color front doors retain the original parameter structure, callback and single cleanup scope. The ordinary observer remains the path for caller templates.

file_and_local_color_p7.published_package: Verified all eight P5 artifact hashes at assets and O:/winnt. The local-style fixture used matching copies of the three released DLLs for each architecture. Only fixture build and package expectations changed.
file_and_local_color_p7.file_selection: 16/16 on the released launcher. ANSI and Unicode, x86 and x64, open and save with both legacy-hook and ordinary Explorer callers. Each passed a relative executable name, its directory as lpstrInitialDir and two filters with index 2 selected. Verified exact full path, nFileOffset, nFileExtension, unchanged process current directory and zero extended error.
file_and_local_color_p7.local_color_style: 2/2 on the real local per-window global-style adapter. The fixture applied Win2000 to its own open native Color dialog and OK control, removed the style, verified the original client size at both transitions, and confirmed the same original RGB. This exercises the callback and lifecycle for a single owned window; the administrative desktop-wide path is still unverified.
file_and_local_color_p7.explorer_resize_limit: On the 427 by 272 work area, SetWindowPos returned success on x86 and x64 but the hooked Explorer client stayed 421 by 247. Bypassing WM_WINDOWPOSCHANGING in an x64 diagnostic raised the client to the intended 555 by 320 offscreen. Native resize anchoring moved the Open button by the same 134 by 73 delta, from (484,313) to (618,386), outside the new client. No production layout relies on bypassing the clamp.
file_and_local_color_p7.print_callback_limit: Native PrintDlgExW with an application-owned IPrintDialogCallback was tested on the ordinary host in both widths, both with and without --2k. All four calls exposed only an external zero-size ProxyModalWindow owned by the fixture. This proxy did not allow a bounded close of the modal call, so the owned fixture was ended at its timeout. Callback dispatch and original-style General page appearance remain inconclusive.

file_buffer_and_print_fallback_p8.file_buffer: 8/8 using the released P5 launcher. A/W open and save on x86/x64 accepted an owned file by relative name with a 16-element buffer. Each returned FALSE and FNERR_BUFFERTOOSMALL, wrote exactly the required 77 elements including the terminator, and preserved the Win2000 frame while open. The file was deleted by the fixture. The package case passes its own scratch directory.
file_buffer_and_print_fallback_p8.custom_print_page: Compared native and released --2k PrintDlgExW with one application-created HPROPSHEETPAGE and that page selected at startup. For both widths the owner saw only an external zero-size ProxyModalWindow. The fixture never observed its page or a same-process print surface and was terminated at the bounded timeout. This does not verify the custom page contract, but the released path did not substitute its in-process bridge.
file_buffer_and_print_fallback_p8.print_owner_chain: A separate x64 comparison walked the visible owner chain up to eight links. The native request exposed only an immediate zero-size proxy and timed out. The ordinary released --2k request exposed its same-process dialog, including range and Apply controls, and returned S_OK with PD_RESULT_CANCEL. The probe acted only on visible nonempty windows linked to its own owner.
file_buffer_and_print_fallback_p8.status: Package artifacts are unchanged. The original General property page and full Explorer layout are still outstanding, as is the administrator desktop path.

places_reflow_trial.package: P9 published launcher and DLLs with temporary caller-owned ANSI and Unicode OPENFILENAME hooks. The probe used the ordinary desktop and owned dialogs at 96 DPI with a 427 by 272 work area. The temporary sources, objects, binaries and output were removed after the run.
places_reflow_trial.stock_geometry: The native 421 by 247 client exposed the stock Places toolbar, a Shell directory view, and a ComboBoxEx filename field. In Open the default OK button began at (484,313), beyond both client bounds.
places_reflow_trial.before_navigation: In a separate x64 trial, all four A/W open and save dialogs fit the directory view, filename edit, both action buttons and the five Places item rectangles. All four returned the expected file, filter index and offsets. The temporary driver reported failure because the stock caller hook intentionally bypassed its compact production-layout assertion.
places_reflow_trial.navigation: Sent button-down and button-up messages to the fourth item in the owned native Places toolbar. The current folder PIDL changed and the owned filename could be entered in all eight A/W open and save cases across x86 and x64. The expected file, filter and offsets were returned in six cases. Both x86 Open cases closed without selecting a file and reported zero extended error. The cached directory-view handle did not yield an in-bounds rectangle after navigation in any case. Buttons, filename field and all five toolbar item bounds still fit.
places_reflow_trial.native_control_p12: The same published package, viewport, hook and toolbar action were tested with the layout changes disabled and enabled. Native Places navigation replaced the directory HWND in 16/16. Reacquiring it showed the new view outside the client for all eight controls and inside it for all eight reflow cases. Opening an absolute filename directly from the virtual folder failed in two x86 controls and one x86 reflow case; x64 returned the expected file in all eight combined cases. The x86 failure therefore also occurs without reflow.
places_reflow_trial.filesystem_return_p12: After the Places action, a second probe entered the owned fixture directory, checked that the current Shell PIDL resolved back to that filesystem directory, and entered the relative filename there. Reflow preserved the file path, filter, offsets and working directory in 8/8 on x86/x64 A/W open/save. The unmodified control passed 7/8; one x86 ANSI Open did not observe the directory return within the bounded check. This does not determine the cause of that intermittent control failure.
places_reflow_trial.dropdown_extents_p12: A separate 8/8 reflow run preserved measured list-window heights for the filename history (219 px), filter (132 px), and drive combo (450 px) before and after placement. This covers native extent retention, not visible menu interaction. All three current diagnostic scratch directories were removed.
places_reflow_trial.pending: Verify repeated navigation and resize, real dropdown and toolbar rendering at applicable DPI, and the caller and product entry policies before integration. Programmatic toolbar messages and control bounds did not verify real mouse, text clipping or a full Win2000 visual match. The published compact path is unchanged.

compact_explorer_p9.reference: Windows 2000 SP2 has two native Explorer templates, including 1547 without a Places toolbar. The Windows 11 no-Places path in both widths still uses SHELLDLL_DefView and a native ComboBoxEx32 filename edit.
compact_explorer_p9.behavior: For a full-size OPENFILENAME Explorer request with no caller hook, template, or multiselect, choose the stock compact variant when the work area can fit it and falls short of the Places layout envelope. The caller's structure and protocol options are preserved across the native call. Native Shell view, filter and selection are retained. The COM single-file bridge uses the same Win32 path.
compact_explorer_p9.fit: At 96 DPI with a 427 by 272 work area, the unadjusted compact Save window measured 436 by 306. Resizing the stock window after it initializes lets its own WM_SIZE handler place the directory view, filename edit, confirm and cancel controls inside the work area. Both the open and save outer bounds then fit 427 by 272.
compact_explorer_p9.scope: The wider Places layout, caller customization, multiselect and smaller work areas use the existing native flow. The metric decision is DPI-normalized; the 427 by 272 at 96 DPI runtime was the measured positive case. A full Places-layout visual match remains outstanding.
compact_explorer_p9.incremental: P5 failed the compact assertion in all eight measured A/W open/save geometry checks. The rebuilt candidate passed Win32 confirmation 16/16 (eight compact and eight legacy), cancellation 16/16, file buffer errors 8/8, and COM and Win16 comparisons 18/18. The 8/8 compact confirmations included preserved caller flags, correct filename and filter output, and unchanged working directory.

verification.compact_fit: 8/8 A/W open/save calls at the measured 427 by 272 work area and 96 DPI. File view, filename and both decision buttons were within the work area. Caller flags, selection path and index, offsets and current directory passed.
